clinical_category: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control

semantic_correction.stem: A nurse explains why hand hygiene is part of a hospital's strategy against antimicrobial-resistant organisms. Which explanation is most accurate?

options.A: Hand hygiene interrupts spread of resistant germs and complements efforts to improve antimicrobial use.
options.B: Hand hygiene reverses bacterial resistance genes after organisms contact alcohol-based sanitizer.
options.C: Hand hygiene replaces antimicrobial stewardship because transmission control alone prevents resistance development.
options.D: Hand hygiene has little effect on resistant-organism spread because healthcare workers' hands are not a transmission route.

semantic_correction.rationale: CDC states that cleaning hands reduces the spread of germs, including germs resistant to antibiotics. CDC's antimicrobial-resistance guidance also emphasizes both stopping the spread of resistant organisms and improving antibiotic and antifungal use. These strategies address different parts of the resistance problem and are complementary. Hand hygiene removes or kills organisms on the hands; it does not genetically reverse resistance, and it does not replace antimicrobial stewardship.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Explain that hand hygiene helps control antimicrobial resistance by interrupting transmission of resistant organisms while antimicrobial stewardship separately improves antimicrobial use.

audit_findings_append.finding: The original answer was uniquely longest. The revised item directly tests transmission interruption and the complementary role of stewardship with balanced alternatives.

option_audit.A: Correct. CDC supports both hand hygiene to reduce resistant-germ spread and improved antimicrobial use to combat resistance.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. Hand hygiene kills or removes organisms; it does not reverse resistance genes.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. Infection prevention and antimicrobial stewardship are complementary strategies rather than substitutes.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. CDC identifies hands and contaminated surfaces as routes by which resistant germs can spread in healthcare.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A alone accurately describes both the transmission-control role of hand hygiene and its relationship to stewardship.
cueing_check: All four options are explanations of hand hygiene and resistance of comparable length and specificity; no unique-length or absolute-word cue identifies A.
